subject: economics
title: Trade Blocs and Globalisation
welcome_lead: Bigger groups, deeper integration - and a backlash too.
meta_desc: A-Level Trade: trade blocs and globalisation winners and losers.
final_note: Trade blocs deepen integration but redistribute jobs and incomes.

concepts.def: Customs union plus free movement of factors.
World Trade Organisation - sets rules since 1995.
New trade between members displacing higher-cost domestic supply.
Trade shifts from low-cost non-members to higher-cost members.

walkthroughs.body_html: From FTA to customs union to single market to monetary union - each step deepens integration and reduces sovereignty over trade and money.
Trade creation raises welfare; trade diversion can lower it. A common external tariff may push imports away from efficient outsiders.
Unevenly shared gains - squeezed manufacturing wages, hollowed-out towns - fuel political backlash, from Brexit to trade wars. Compensating losers is essential to sustain free trade.

mcqs.q: A customs union differs from a free trade area by:
options: Common external tariff
Free movement of people
Shared currency
No internal tariffs
Trade shifting from low-cost non-members to higher-cost members
All new trade among members
Tariffs disappearing entirely
Increased dumping

mcqs.q: What is the principle of comparative advantage?
options: Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.
Comparative advantage means richer countries should help poorer ones.
Countries should specialise in producing goods with lower opportunity cost relative to others — even a country worse at everything still has a comparative advantage in something.
A country should produce whatever it can make best.

mcqs.q: Is a trade deficit necessarily bad?
options: A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
A trade deficit always means a country is losing wealth and failing economically.
Not necessarily — it can reflect strong domestic demand, attractive investment opportunities, or borrowing to fund growth. Context matters more than the headline figure.
Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.

mcqs.q: Why do economists generally argue against protectionism?
options: A trade deficit means a country has no factories.
Protectionism always makes a country richer by keeping money at home.

Tariffs and quotas raise prices for consumers, protect inefficient industries, invite retaliation, and reduce overall welfare — even when they save specific jobs, the cost per job saved typically exceeds the wage.
Protectionism means protecting national parks from development.
